source.title: Discovering Interpretable Acoustic Features in Autoregressive Voice-Cloning TTS Models
source.authors: Anuj Diwan; David Harwath; Eunsol Choi

record.tranche_reason: Extends SAE-based feature analysis to autoregressive voice-cloning TTS models, measuring how well dictionary features predict acoustic concepts; it does not test the toy-model superposition geometry itself.
record.gate_note: The paper measures SAE feature recoverability and validates labels for TTS features. It does not measure feature overlap, near-orthogonality, capacity competition, or neuron polysemanticity. Probing and steering results are included only where they bear on sparse SAE-recoverable features. Figure-only numerical values are not transcribed as exact values.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK SAEs on residual streams of six autoregressive voice-cloning TTS backbones. It compares them with PCA, random directions and untrained SAEs on sparse probing and on quantitative auto-interpretability. This bears on V4's claim that real transformer models contain sparse features an SAE can recover, in a new setting: speech-token language models, not text LLMs. It does not test toy-model geometry, capacity, polysemanticity, completeness or canonicity, or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state that PCA and random directions are strong probing baselines, and that PCA is competitive for dense probing and steering. They add that strong sparse probing does not always translate to steering, and they report 684 validated SAE features in Qwen3-TTS.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and evaluates TopK SAEs on voice-cloning TTS residual-stream activations; it does not reproduce the original toy-network setup or its geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Sparse recoverability varies by concept and model; in Qwen3-TTS it varies by layer, with sparse recoverability stronger in later layers. Auto-interpretability was evaluated only at Qwen3-TTS layer 19.

fits_no_version.finding: Random directions give near-zero steering target change despite competitive probing. SAE steering is competitive with PCA in Qwen3-TTS and Fish but severely degrades speech in Higgs TTS 3. Sparse recoverability correlates weakly with steering effect (Spearman 0.20/0.22 in Qwen, about 0 in Fish).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features that predict a concept are not reliably causal levers for it in the model.

record.problems: The study concerns voice-cloning TTS rather than general-purpose LLMs and does not measure superposition geometry or feature overlap. The paper notes that Gemini generates and evaluates labels, so its automated metrics alone are not independent ground-truth validation; human label-fit evaluation is reported only for a subset. Several probing comparisons are given qualitatively in the text or as figures rather than exact numerical values.

untested.parts: No toy networks, feature overlap or orthogonality measurement, sparsity transition, or geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions, or neuron polysemanticity.
No analysis of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Not tested in general-purpose text LLMs, and no measure of features spread across neurons; only SAE recoverability in TTS backbones.
Label stability concerns the stability of Gemini's labels, not of SAE features across seeds or sizes. Completeness and canonicity are not tested.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: PCA and random directions have higher all-feature extractor-concept recoverability than SAE across all six models.
Human Label Fit is 64.4% for validated vs 51.0% for non-validated SAE features (50 each). Random directions approach SAE on Label Fit (0.60 vs 0.63).
Comparison against untrained SAE features in probing (a key control for whether trained dictionaries recover real structure).

record.verdict_notes: The setting is TTS autoregressive backbones, not text LLMs, so V4 is supported only by extension to speech-token LMs. Auto-interpretability is single-layer and single-model, and Gemini both generates and scores the labels. Most probing numbers are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: No test of overcomplete toy networks, overlapping or nearly orthogonal feature directions, sparsity-dependent geometric transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemantic neurons.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Tests SAE-based recovery of acoustic concepts in voice-cloning TTS models, not feature spreading across neurons or recovery in general-purpose LLMs; does not test superposition geometry.
Label coherence, predictive fit, and relabeling consistency do not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of the model.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: six TTS models (aggregate across models)
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized F1 from top-2 features for human-labelled concepts across SAE and PCA feature sets.

conditions.value: Qwen3-TTS, Fish S1-mini, Fish S2 Pro, Higgs TTS 2, Higgs TTS 3, CosyVoice2

rows.value: SAE exceeds PCA across all six models
rows.note: The paper reports the cross-model comparison qualitatively; exact means are shown only in a figure.
rows.check: Correct as recorded. SAE top-2 nF1 for 21 human-labelled concepts exceeds PCA in all six models; Fig. 13 shows this at k=2, 5 and 10. Values appear only in figures.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 3.2–3.3; Figure 3 caption; Appendix E.2, Figure 13.

rows.baseline: Other tested models; exact values not stated
rows.value: SAE leads in sparse extractor-concept recoverability only in Qwen3-TTS
rows.note: The stated result indicates model dependence; exact model-level values are in the figure.
rows.check: Correct. SAE leads top-2 extractor-concept recoverability only in Qwen3-TTS. The baseline should read 'PCA/random/untrained SAE in the same model', not 'other tested models'.

source_check.correct: Baseline: PCA, random directions and untrained SAE within each model, rather than other tested models. SAE leads top-2 extractor-concept recovery only in Qwen3-TTS; exact means are not stated in prose.

rows.subject: Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated prediction of known concepts from the full feature set and from only two features.

conditions.value: SAE, PCA, random directions, untrained SAE

rows.measure: Normalized F1 recoverability from two features versus all features
rows.baseline: All-feature recovery; exact values not stated
rows.value: Many concepts are recoverable, but few are sparsely predicted from two features; extractor concepts are generally more recoverable than human-labelled concepts
rows.note: The paper does not give exact values for this summary in the text.
rows.check: This summary pools all feature sets; it is not an SAE-specific result. It bears on V4 only loosely, as evidence that many concepts are not sparsely encoded. The baseline is all-feature recoverability, and values are figure-only.

rows.subject: Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Auto-interpreted SAE features and retained those passing the stated coherence, label-fit, and label-stability thresholds.
rows.measure: Count of automatically validated SAE features
rows.value: 92 validated features among the initial 500; 592 additional validated SAE features were found among remaining eligible features, for 684 total
rows.note: This supports the presence of SAE features with validated audio labels in this TTS model, but does not show that the dictionary is complete or canonical.
rows.check: Correct. 92 of 500 SAE features were validated, versus 17 random and 1 PCA, plus 592 more for 684 total. The validation uses the same Gemini model for labelling and scoring. 'numbers_found: 5/5' is spurious; the coherence threshold is 3/5.

relationships.condition: Sparse probing of human-labelled concepts across six TTS models; auto-interpretability at Qwen3-TTS layer 19
relationships.reason: SAE beats PCA on top-2 human-concept recovery in all six models (r1). SAE yields far more validated interpretable features than PCA or random directions (r4), and human Label Fit is 64.4% vs 51.0% for validated vs non-validated features (text, Sec. 4.2).
relationships.display_finding: SAEs beat PCA on top-2 recovery of human-labelled concepts in all six models and gave far more validated interpretable features than PCA or random directions. Human Label Fit was 64.4% for validated versus 51.0% for non-validated features.

relationships.condition: Extractor-concept probing, and sparse (top-2) recovery generally
relationships.reason: SAE leads top-2 extractor recovery only in Qwen3-TTS (r2), and few concepts are sparsely recoverable (r3). Per the text (Sec. 3.3; no row), PCA and random directions beat SAE on all-feature extractor recoverability in every model.
relationships.display_finding: The SAE led top-2 extractor recovery only in Qwen3-TTS, and few concepts were sparsely recoverable. PCA and random directions beat the SAE on all-feature extractor recoverability in every model.

tranche.reason: Tests sparse feature recovery and interpretability in a new setting: autoregressive voice-cloning TTS residual streams across six models.

source_check.notes: Automatic validation uses Gemini 3.5 Flash for both labeling and scoring; human evaluation independently checks a subset. r3 summarizes recovery across feature sets, rather than an SAE-specific failure; these results do not establish complete or canonical dictionary units.

statements.correction: Qwen3-TTS layer 19: 500 features sampled per feature set; 92 SAE, 17 random-direction and 1 PCA features pass validation. Status: preprint under review. Controls and 95% bootstrap intervals reported. Introduction: code release planned.
statements.problem: The feature counts and setting are correct, but the text promises a future code release rather than establishing that code is available.
